description: Western counter-strategies: minerals-for-security, arbitration, technological exploration
verification_status: substantially updated relative to the user's original documents - the US-DRC deal has gone much further than a mere 'proposal'; it is a signed agreement as of mid-2026

timeline.event: Tshisekedi's first public offer (NYT interview) - mineral access in exchange for help against M23
formal proposal from the Trump administration; Tshisekedi also sends a letter to Trump
Erik Prince/FSG contract with the DRC Ministry of Finance (~$700m)
DRC and Rwanda foreign ministers sign a peace declaration in Washington
Tshisekedi and Kagame in Washington: the Washington Accords (peace) plus the US-DRC Strategic Partnership (minerals and security) are signed
Congolese lawyers file a constitutional challenge against the agreement in Kinshasa
criticism grows: Tshisekedi's office praises the partnership but fighting continues; Corneille Nangaa (AFC/M23) calls the deal 'unconstitutional'
Virtus Minerals (US, 8 employees) - the first major deal under the program: rights to the Mutoshi deposit (up to 5% of world cobalt supply)

minerals_for_security.deal_terms: preferential access for American firms to DRC minerals (cobalt, copper, lithium, tantalum) in exchange for security assistance, training, equipment, and transport-corridor development
criticism: Oakland Institute (report 'Shafted', Oct 2025): peace is being 'sacrificed' for extraction
Al Jazeera (Feb 2026): Congolese fear a repeat of the exploitative model
Public Citizen: the deal expands investor rights with weak accountability safeguards

erik_prince_details.background: FSG had registered entities in the DRC since 2018; in 2023 the UN Group of Experts accused Prince of attempting to bring 2,500 Latin American mercenaries into North Kivu (the deal fell through)
erik_prince_details.2025_contract: finalized before M23's January 2025 offensive began; focused on tax collection and anti-smuggling, with no initial plan for combat involvement
erik_prince_details.source: Reuters (exclusive by Jessica Donati, Sonia Rolley)

manono_arbitration.parties: AVZ Minerals (Australia) vs. DRC/Cominiere; a parallel dispute with Zijin Mining

timeline.event: DRC's Ministry of Justice revokes AVZ's permit (PE13359), transferring the asset to a structure involving Zijin
ICSID interim measures favor recognizing the rights of Dathcom Mining (AVZ's structure)
the ICC awards AVZ EUR39.1m (~$42.46m) - compensation from Cominiere for breaching interim measures; this is NOT a ruling on the merits of the underlying dispute
AVZ and KoBold Metals sign a framework agreement (~$1bn) brokered by the US - an attempt to settle AVZ's claims
ICSID proceedings suspended until 23 June at the US's request
AVZ resumes ICSID arbitration - the DRC did not engage in substantive dialogue
per IDS reporting, the White House pushes AVZ to sell its interests to KoBold Metals
CAMI (DRC's registry) cancels AVZ's related permit (PR 4029) for unpaid fees
the Zijin/Cominiere JV ('Manono Lithium', 61%/39%) begins the DRC's first lithium production

manono_arbitration.key_clarification: the $42m award is an ICC ruling against Cominiere for a specific procedural breach - NOT a final ruling on the merits of the ownership dispute; the main ICSID case against the DRC state remains ongoing as of 2026

kobold_metals.role_in_manono: framework agreement to buy out AVZ's stake (May 2025, ~$1bn) with US backing
kobold_metals.verification_status: the general profile is well documented; the detailed financial structure of the Manono deal was not verified beyond the cited sources

virtus_minerals.profile: American company, 8 employees at the time of the deal
virtus_minerals.deal: rights to copper-cobalt deposits including Mutoshi (a former Chemaf asset) - up to 5% of world cobalt supply
virtus_minerals.significance: the first major deal signed after the December 2025 US-DRC agreement
virtus_minerals.nuance: the Mutoshi asset was previously (2024) the target of a competing $1.4bn bid from China's Norin Mining (Norinco) - it ultimately went to the American company
